summary.headline: RHI Magnesita India Q2 FY27 revenue ₹1,030 crore with EBITDA margin of 14% (up 332 bps YoY) on value-over-volume strategy.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about ₹1,030 crore, the second consecutive quarter above ₹1,000 crore, and EBITDA was ₹144 crore at a 14% margin, up 332 bps YoY. PAT rose 62% YoY to ₹62 crore. Management said it deliberately stepped away from low-margin orders, which kept volumes lower but supported realisations. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹2,044 crore (+2% YoY), EBITDA ₹291 crore (+36%), margin 14.2% (+353 bps), and PAT ₹127 crore (+72%). Working capital rose to 38% of revenue on inventory build, and H1 operating cash flow was ₹99 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Second consecutive quarter above ₹1,000 crore; QoQ change not quantified
Stated as positive despite working capital build

segments.name: Flow control products
segments.commentary: Management said flow control sales grew in pieces rather than tonnes, lifting realisation and masking raw-material cost increases in the material cost percentage. Mix shift toward flow control was described as more than 3 bps QoQ, which appears to be a transcription error.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Management chose not to bid on some cement opportunities it judged low value, which the company said explains the large YoY gap in this segment. It said it still won some large maintenance and project orders.

segments.name: Silica / cocoon (co-pro)
segments.commentary: Company says it received its largest co-pro order in history to supply silica production lines for 18 months; management said it will take more than a year to execute and will lift utilisation of its silica and quartzite plants.

guidance_outlook: No revenue or realisation guidance given; management said Q2 realisation is likely an anomaly from stepping away from low-margin orders.
FY28 medium-term outlook reiterated: volume growth of about 7% and margin around 14%, per an analyst's summary. Management did not confirm a 15-18% revenue growth target.

Captive raw material: Chirya Pani quartzite mine (40,000 tpa) is operating; Vikampalli mine is expected to start next quarter. Dolomite / DBM backward integration is in its initial phase, with full captive supply targeted in about a year.
Project orders are expected to return in H2 FY27, with a healthy pipeline and higher margins than standard orders.
capex_capacity: Quartzite / Chirya Pani mine operational at 40,000 tpa annual capacity; Vikampalli mine start-up expected next quarter.
Captive raw material via the new raw-material facility started operations near quarter-end; savings estimated at 3–3.5% of raw-material cost, with full captive supply targeted in about a year.
Minpro joint venture with Khemka Refractories started invoicing in August 2026; capacity expansion planned next quarter.
Capacity utilisation is in the low 60s%. No volume guidance given.
Capex is directed at equipment reliability upgrades, technology transfers from the global parent, and compliance; figures were not given.
demand_pricing: Realisations rose as the mix shifted to flow control and the company declined low-margin orders, mainly in cement. Management declined to guide on realisation.
Raw material costs are rising: magnesia, DBM and fused magnesia have sharply increased, with a recent steep rise in DBM and FM prices, alumina-based inputs also up, and ocean freight higher.
Indian steel demand grew about 7.2% in H1 while crude steel output grew about 2.8%, per management.
Competition: Chinese suppliers remain a concern in cocoon; management expects India's refractory overcapacity to persist for a while.
Export: management said North America is not feasible; Europe is uncompetitive due to CBAM; Middle East and Africa are the only near-term export opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key focus areas for the new CEO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new steel product opportunities (CSP trial with a large Indian account), penetration of leading partner markets, domestic sourcing shifts, the recycling business, and digital customer reach.

qa_highlights.question: How will the captive raw-material (quartzite) facility affect costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said savings are estimated at 3–3.5% of raw-material cost, with full captive supply expected in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the volume growth guidance of 7–9% be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is balancing value and volume and did not give a new number, but acknowledged the need to improve volumes and expects project orders to contribute in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise and working capital intensity increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose due to raw-material cost inflation, building stock for large silica orders, industrial project orders, and resilience buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue grow 15–18% from FY28 while margins hold at 14–15%?
qa_highlights.answer: No forward revenue guidance was given. Management reiterated growth drivers in glass, gasifiers, industrial segments and technology transfers, and said it is working toward FY28 growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing market share given flat revenue around ₹1,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the flow control business is gaining share and some orders will flow through later. It said cement was deliberately under-bid, and it pointed to a plan to rebuild share through solution-based selling.

risks_watch: Raw-material and freight inflation (magnesia, DBM, FM, alumina) may pressure margins despite pass-through efforts.
Working capital intensity at 38% and inventory build need to unwind for cash conversion to improve.
Volume is lagging; the 7–9% volume growth target was not reaffirmed, and capacity utilisation is in the low 60s%.
Chinese competition in cocoon and industry overcapacity may keep pricing under pressure.
CFO transition to Abhishek Bajaj; the Vikampalli mine start and project-order timing in H2 are key items to monitor.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and profitability, with the margin gain attributed to value-over-volume choices and mix. Evasive on volume, realisation and revenue-growth targets, which management declined to guide on. Cautious on cement, export and industrial recovery.
key_quotes: Despite a challenging operating environment, we delivered second consecutive quarter with revenue exceeding 1000 crores and a beta margin of 14%.
We chose value generating orders which is sustainable and most importantly strengthen solutions based selling to our customers.
Graduate would be fully captive this is what we're working on right.

growth.why: No revenue guidance; management declined to guide on realisation and dropped the volume-growth number, while H1 revenue grew only 2% YoY with utilisation in the low 60s%. Backing is partial: a 40,000 tpa mine and a silica co-pro order for 18 months, with project orders expected back in H2 FY27 and raw-material captive savings of 3–3.5%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin was 14% (+332 bps YoY) and H1 was 14.2% (+353 bps), driven by flow-control mix, declining low-margin cement orders, and captive quartzite savings of 3-3.5% of raw-material cost, though raw-material inflation (magnesia, DBM, FM) is a headwind.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Vikampalli quartzite mine start and Minpro JV capacity expansion are both planned for next quarter, but these are raw-material and small JV adds with no size given, and utilisation is only in the low 60s%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management dropped the 7-9% volume target and declined to guide; H1 revenue grew only 2% YoY and utilisation is in the low 60s%, with project orders only expected back in H2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is in the low 60s%, well below the 80%+ level that would prompt a new capacity announcement, and capex is directed at reliability, technology transfer and compliance with no growth figure given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or realisation guidance was given, the volume-growth target was not reaffirmed, and management said the Q2 realisation is likely an anomaly rather than a trend to build on.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Volume is lagging with utilisation in the low 60s%, the 7-9% volume target was dropped, and raw-material inflation (DBM, FM, magnesia, freight) could pressure margins even as project orders are expected back in H2 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited a CSP trial with a large Indian steel account and growth in glass, gasifiers and industrial segments, but gave no launch dates or sizes.

rows.label: Silica/cocoon co-pro order for 18 months
rows.why: Largest co-pro order in company history to supply silica production lines for 18 months, with execution over more than a year and expected to lift silica and quartzite plant utilisation.

rows.label: Project orders return
rows.why: Management expects project orders to return in H2 FY27 at higher margins than standard orders, supported by a healthy pipeline, though no value was given.

rows.label: Captive raw-material savings
rows.why: Savings estimated at 3-3.5% of raw-material cost as the new facility started near quarter-end, with full captive supply targeted in about a year.
